text:
sam: Hey team - noticed another long-running job saw KV cache memory climb ~18% over 8h with heavy long-context chat. heap profile looks like lots of small free holes that never get reused, fragmentationy. attaching quick profiler dump below and a couple ideas.

marta: ugh that matches the telemetry from the canary we rolled yesterday. saw tail latency + few OOM traces on the 0400 window.

li: can you paste the pprof snippet?

sam: pasted. skimmed output:
```
pprof: top 10 allocs (kv-cache)
  34.2%  34.2%  0xabc...    small_slots_alloc
  28.1%  62.3%  0xdef...    slot_split
  12.0%  74.3%  0x123...    slab_fragment_scan
  5.3%   79.6%  0x456...    mark_reuse_miss
```
Looks like allocator is doing lots of splits for small tails and we have high scatter of free fragments.

alex: Are these fragments primarily under 256B? Last time we saw similar behavior when the block_size knob was 4KB/512B mix.

sam: Yes, >70% fragments <512B. Current allocator bins are [64,128,256,512,1024,4096]. We get lots of 256->split->64/192-ish waste.

ben: Two quick axes: change bin sizes (coarser lower bins) or background compaction that stitches adjacent free slots (best-effort cheap merge). Stitching costs memcopy and CPU but avoids big pauses if we do it in tiny windows.

marta: I like stitching + heuristics: only attempt on contiguous free runs >= 1KB and when CPU budget < X. avoids thrashing.

li: what about buddy allocator? Would give O(1) coalescing but increases internal fragmentation for asymmetric workloads. Also harder to implement incrementally because we need power-of-two alignment.

sam: thought about hybrid: keep small slab allocator for tiny slots, but add a background "stitcher" that walks recent-freed lists and tries to coalesce adjacent holes into larger free blocks. It would maintain a lightweight index of free runs per slab page.

alex: Could we detect long-context workloads and switch to larger block profile (e.g., bump min block 256->512) dynamically per worker? Kind of per-route allocator hints.

ben: yes. route-based tuning + stitcher seems promising. Also we can add a metric: kv.stitch_attempts, kv.stitch_success, kv.split_waste_bytes. Get histograms for hole sizes.

sam: prototype plan:
- add a background worker (low priority, capped CPU) that merges adjacent free fragments when runqueue idle
- add per-slab compact watermark: only trigger if free_fragment_ratio > 0.2 and avg_hole_size < 512
- add runtime flags: `--kv-stitch-window=30s --kv-stitch-cpu-pct=5`
- telemetry: emit kv.frag_ratio, kv.avg_hole, kv.stitch_ms_per_run

marta: can you sketch a minimal API for the stitcher? would be handy for review.

sam: quick sketch:
```go
// on free: append to freeRuns[page].push({offset, len, ts})
// stitcher loop: for page in pages {
//   runs := freeRuns[page].snapshot()
//   sort by offset
//   walk and merge adjacent runs if gap==0 or gap < threshold
//   if mergedLen >= minCompactSize { put merged back into free list as single block }
// }
```
Ben: keep gap threshold configurable. also ensure we don't hold page locks long - do snapshot then CAS the replacement.

li: we should test with a synthetic workload that alternates long contexts and short bursts; instrument with heap snapshots and failure injection. I can write a driver.

alex: also consider doing compaction opportunistically during KV cache checkpoint/eviction flow: when we evict cold entries we may create contiguous free space, so try to opportunistically stitch there to avoid separate pass.

marta: ops-bot FYI: can we schedule a canary with `kv-stitcher` feature flag on 3 nodes next weekday?

ops-bot: scheduled canary: rollout=kv-stitcher-canary, nodes=3, start=1717860000 (unix ts), notify=@eng-runtime.

sam: thanks. Next steps: li will write the driver + synthetic tests, sam will prototype stitcher with flags, ben will add metrics + dashboards. We'll reconvene after first bench.

ben: quick note: if stitcher isn't enough we might need periodic compaction (copy-compact) for worst-case fragmentation. that's heavier but can be rate-limited per-node.

marta: cool. small bikeshed: name the feature `kv-stitcher` or `kv-defragger`? I prefer stitcher.

li: stitcher it is. I'll ping when tests are ready. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks all.
